author: Penry Buckley
description:
State planning minister declares project ‘state significant’, wresting approval process away from local council

Plans for a grand new public square in centre of Sydney are in doubt after the New South Wales planning minister declared the project “state significant”, wresting the approval process away from the City of Sydney.

The lord mayor, Clover Moore, released renders in August for the plaza opposite Sydney’s town hall. The design for the space, which the council had expected to be completed by 2031, include a semi-circular clearing projecting eastwards towards Hyde park, with a fountain and a grove of native trees.

Continue reading...
title: Plans for Sydney’s controversial new public square in doubt after NSW government intervention

author: Sam Levin
description:
Agents surrounded the man and child in his car before firing multiple rounds, according to Zohran Mamdani

A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man in New York City on Thursday afternoon, according to the city’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani.

Early reports indicated that agents had surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds, the mayor said in a statement on Thursday evening. The child was physically unharmed, according to Mamdani.

Continue reading...
title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old nearby, mayor says

author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
description:
Prof Peter Fonagy’s 607-page report is categoric that mental distress has increased substantially and ‘cannot be explained by greater awareness alone’

  • Full report | NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

  • Analysis | No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

The Fonagy review of NHS England’s mental health, ADHD and autism services was commissioned in 2025 by Wes Streeting, then the health secretary, in response to growing concerns that spiralling waiting lists for assessment, diagnosis and care threatened the NHS’s ability to meet the demand.

The 607-page report,
title: NHS England mental health services review: what has it found and what does it recommend?

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Peter Fonagy lauds courage of young people and warns of consequences of rising prevalence of mental illness

  • Full report | NHS at risk of ‘system failures’ as demand for ADHD and autism care soars, inquiry finds

  • Explainer | What has the Fonagy review found and what does it recommend?

Eighteen months ago, in an off-the-cuff remark during a discussion on disability benefit cuts, Wes Streeting said mental health conditions were being “overdiagnosed”, riding headlong into another culture war.

He later apologised for the comment, but at the time it seemed the then health secretary h
title: No ‘snowflakes’: mental health review says today’s youth have it harder and harms are real

author: Associated Press
description:
Flowers, tried six times over 1996 murders of four people, faced execution before supreme court tossed his conviction

Curtis Flowers, a Black man who spent more than 22 years in prison and was on death row in Mississippi before the US supreme court threw out his conviction and death sentence, has died. He was 56.

Flowers’ family confirmed that he died on Wednesday at his home in Mississippi, attorney Rob McDuff told the Associated Press on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Curtis Flowers, US man wrongfully imprisoned for 22 years, dies aged 56

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
The $11-a-share offer would have been the biggest debut on the stock market since the telecommunication giant in 1997

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Firmus Technologies has scrapped what was set to be Australia’s biggest company listing in decades after investor demand for its much-hyped AI datacentre business failed to materialise.

A Firmus spokesperson said the board decided that proceeding with the offer was no longer in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.

Continue reading...
title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Chris Murphy says Pentagon blocked him from military base in Qatar and Iran strike on US embassy in Riyadh far worse than public led to believe

The US senator Chris Murphy said the Pentagon blocked him from a major US base in Qatar, yet saw enough damage on the US embassy in Saudi Arabia to conclude that an Iranian strike would have been deadly had it happened during the day.

The Connecticut Democrat, who sits on the Senate foreign relations and appropriations committees, described the destruction he witnessed in Riyadh as “extraordinary” and much more damaging than the public has been led to believe.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic senator says Hegseth trying to hide costs of Iran war from US public

author: Sam Levine
description:
Cassidy Hutchinson told panel she had been told Trump lunged for wheel of SUV to try to join mob at Capitol

Prosecutors in the justice department’s civil rights division are seeking criminal charges against Cassidy Hutchinson, a former top Trump White House aide who gave explosive testimony to the committee that investigated the US attack on the Capitol, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The potential charges involve lying to Congress, the person said.

Continue reading...
title: DoJ seeks to charge ex-Trump aide who gave key testimony on January 6 attack

author: Donna Lu
description:
Intense flash of radio waves is more than 10bn years old and has travelled through ‘approximately 80% of cosmic history’

A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away, a mysterious flash of energy was released into the universe.

Astronomers have now detected that flash, a burst of radio waves which travelled for more than 10bn years before reaching Earth – what they believe to be the most distant fast radio burst (FRB) ever recorded.

Continue reading...
title: Astronomers detect mysterious burst of energy from a galaxy far, far away

author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
description:
Lawyer for CNN, MS Now and Politico says Trump admitted he banned networks from White House over their coverage

Donald Trump continues to be the strongest witness for the media companies arguing that they were unfairly barred from the White House at his direction, a lawyer representing CNN, MS Now and Politico told a federal judge on Thursday afternoon.

The media coalition was in court asking the judge to extend the temporary restraining order (TRO) he issued on 24 September requiring the White House to lift the ban for 14 days. That temporary reprieve was scheduled to expire on Thursday, but district court judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, said he would extend it until Tuesday and that he would likely rule on a motion for a preliminary injunction by that day. That means the White House will be forced to allow journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to continue accessing the building until at least Tuesday.
title: Trump made ‘clear’ that media ban was due to critical coverage, lawyer tells judge

author: Reuters
description:
Move would reunite chief executive Brian Niccol with chain he led before joining coffee company two years ago

Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, in a move that ⁠would reunite chief executive Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led before joining the coffee giant two years ago.

The potential deal comes as restaurant chains wrestle with uncertain demand from inflation-weary ⁠consumers and rising operating costs, prompting ⁠companies to look ​for new avenues of growth while facing pressure to improve profitability.

Continue reading...
title: Starbucks reportedly exploring Chipotle takeover

author: Ariana Baio
description:
US ambassador to Greece allegedly asked Trump donor to pay $100,000 American Express bill

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, brushed off reporters’ questions about recent reports that Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece and Trump family ally, used her position to advance personal interests.

Rubio refused to respond to the latest allegations against Guilfoyle, raised in a Wall Street Journal report, claiming she asked a Trump donor to pay her $100,000 American Express bill in exchange for access to the administration, before her US senate confirmation hearing.

Continue reading...
title: Marco Rubio brushes off questions about Kimberly Guilfoyle pressing donor to pay credit card

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
Vice-president also says Adobe is barred from visa program that allows high-skilled workers to apply for US residency

Microsoft is suspended from applying for permanent residency for workers employed through a US visa program for high-skilled workers, JD Vance announced on Thursday.

The US vice-president accused the tech company of abusing the H-1B system, which allows those on the visa to work while they apply and are in process for a green card.

Continue reading...
title: Microsoft suspended from applying for green cards for H-1B workers, JD Vance says

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Lawyers for Wells’s family have called for a federal investigation into 18-year-old’s disappearance and death

On Wednesday, Donald Trump said he was considering asking the FBI to investigate the death of Nolan Wells, a Black college freshman who was last seen alive on a 4 July boating trip with friends.

Wells, 18, went missing while on Horn Island, a barrier island off the coast of Mississippi. His body was found on the island two days later. Wells’s cause and manner of death are still undetermined.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says he is considering asking FBI to investigate the death of Nolan Wells

author: Anna Betts
description:
Residents in areas from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Florida urged to ‘evacuate if told to do so’

Millions of people from Louisiana to Florida are under hurricane warnings on Thursday as Hurricane Isaias looked set to head towards the US Gulf coast with weather officials warning of dangerous storm surge, hurricane-force winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding.

Isaias intensified into a hurricane from a tropical storm on Wednesday night, becoming the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.

Continue reading...
title: Hurricane Isaias forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, with millions under warnings in US

author: Josh Butler
description:
The inflammatory clip shows the wild west of online politicking created by unrestricted access to AI – and why watchdogs need more powers to do something about it

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation’s new AI-generated campaign video is a new low – even for them.

The video – reportedly played at the party’s Victorian campaign launch over the weekend – is an AI-generated collection of racist tropes, depicting a man who appears to be African brandishing a machete, an apparently Middle Eastern man with an explosive vest, a South Asian man in a turban tal
title: One Nation’s AI video is vile and tired – but the ensloppification of Australian politics doesn’t stop there

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
Recovery marks a dramatic turnaround for Pike, who remains in hospital after a botched execution in Tennessee

Christa Pike is “up and walking” in hospital, her lawyer said, just more than a week after she survived two lethal injections during a botched execution in Tennessee.

The recovery marks a dramatic turnaround after Pike was declared brain dead on Monday, before waking up and beginning to speak on Tuesday. Her ordeal has shocked many in the US and overseas and galvanized critics of the death penalty.

Continue reading...
title: Christa Pike is ‘up and walking’ for first time after failed execution, lawyer says

author: Martin Belam
description:
The president was repeatedly interrupted at a rally and faces a legal challenge over taxpayer-funded adverts. Plus Jonathan, the giant tortoise who may have the secret to longevity

Good morning. Donald Trump suffered a torrid night at a rally in Texas that was rocked by repeated protests. The US president briefly stepped away from the microphone after one protester appeared to approach the stage. At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted Trump during his remarks in San Antonio, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by an older Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena.

What is the latest development in the saga over taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads? The Democratic National Committee has sued the Trump administration
title: First Thing: Trump endures protests in Texas as DNC sues over adverts

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Wren Michelle Roberts was born with heterotaxy, a syndrome so rare a specialist could only find 15 similar cases

South-eastern Louisiana couple Nick and Savannah Roberts planned to bury their infant daughter the weekend after she was born in September with an exceedingly rare combination of birth defects that her doctors feared was unsurvivable.

But an unforeseen congenital trait in Wren Michelle Roberts’ heart, combined with her parents’ dedication to her complex medical care, has allowed her to defy her bleak initial prognosis and meet weeks’ worth of milestones that each are a “miracle in [their] own way”, according to her doctor.

Continue reading...
title: US infant defies bleak odds from rare congenital trait: ‘Don’t quit before your child quits’

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Devastating blaze near Sizewell B nuclear power station in Suffolk among a record 624 wildfires in July this year

This July was the worst on record for wildfires in England, provisional data shows, with England experiencing a clear upward trend in the total number of wildfires recorded.

This summer has been a stark reminder of the vulnerability of the UK to climate breakdown, after punishingly hot and dry weather turned large parts of the countryside into a tinderbox.

Continue reading...
title: July 2026 was worst on record for wildfires in England, data shows

author: Sian Cain
description:
Lenora Thaker wins $30,000 prize for ‘a work of state significance’ for The Pearl of Tagai Town, which draws on her family’s history in Cairns-Malay Town

A “stunning” debut novel described as “unambiguously and distinctively Queensland” has won the $30,000 top prize at the Queensland literary awards (QLAs).

Meriam and Wagedagam author Lenora Thaker won the Queensland premier’s award for a work of state significance for her historical novel The Pearl of Tagai Town, which was inspired by her ancestors’ lives in an unmapped shantytown known as Cairns-Malay Town. The town once housed Indigenous Australians, Chinese, Indian, Japanese, Malaysian and Sri Lankan residents who had been segregated from the white population; it existed from the late 1800s until the late 1950s.
title: Queensland literary awards: ‘stunning’ debut inspired by segregated shantytown wins top prize

author: Chris Stein in Lima, Ohio
description:
Ohio former senator attacks Republican rival as the ‘face of datacenters’ as he wraps AI concerns into pro-worker message

Sherrod Brown, the Democratic former senator from Ohio hoping to return to office in November’s midterm elections, has spent the past year traveling across his home state explaining to voters about all the ways the “system is rigged” against them. Recently, he’s been telling people about a trip he took across the north-west Ohio countryside.

“You’re driving on what looks like really good farmland, driving past fields, driving past barns, driving past milking parlors, and you see, all of a sudden, you see these huge cranes and you see these trucks coming,” Brown told a crowd of dozens at a coffee shop in the city of Lima earlier this month.

Continue reading...
title: ‘System is rigged’: Democrat Sherrod Brown puts datacenter danger at heart of populist Senate bid

author: Anna Betts
description:
Deployment for nearly a year was marked by reports of supply shortages, and deteriorating morale and mental health among crew

The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon.

It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages, and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members.
title: USS Abraham Lincoln scheduled to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Talks between Sainsbury’s and Morrisons have set industry tongues wagging, with analysts saying the market is ripe for change

  • Tesco lifts profit forecast and says shoppers are resilient

  • Business live – latest updates

They may be two of the most recognisable brands in Britain, with a combined 188 years serving shoppers, but industry watchers agree that either Asda or Morrisons – or both – could disappear within a decade.

This week, it emerged that Sainsbury’s and Morrisons – the UK’s second- and sixth-largest supermarket chains – had held merger talks between
title: Supermarket shake-up: why Asda or Morrisons could vanish within a decade

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Vessel spent over 260 consecutive days at sea without a port call, a US navy record

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

The USS Abraham Lincoln will return home to San Diego later today after supporting the Iran war during a record long deployment of 265 uninterrupted days at sea.

In remarks in San Antonio, Texas, Donald Trump tried to channel the anti-Muslim racism that helped get him elected in 2016, by skipping straight from a dire warning that Iran would use a nuclear weapon if it had one to the wild, false claim that Barack Obama could have stopped the Ft Hood gunman, Nidal Hasan, but chose not to.

Trump repeated his false claim that the war he started with Iran in February was necessary to prevent Iran from destroying American cities like Los Angeles or San Diego in a nuclear attack. In fact, US intelligence agencies assessed in
title: USS Lincoln carrier to return to port in San Diego after record-breaking deployment – US politics live

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Global bond market sell-off continues and stocks fall amid another wave of potential strikes against Iran

  • Business live – latest updates

Oil prices have risen sharply amid fears about escalating tensions in the Middle East and a squeeze on production from the threat of a hurricane off the US coast.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3.8% to $104 a barrel on Thursday, triggering a wave of selling in the global bond and stock markets.

Continue reading...
title: Oil prices rise sharply on Middle East tensions and US hurricane threat

author: Taz Ali
description:
Voters choosing replacement for Keir Starmer, who announced he was standing down last month

Good morning and welcome to our UK politics live blog.

Polls have opened in Keir Starmer’s old seat in Holborn and St Pancras, where the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, is hoping to break Labour’s longstanding grip in the north London constituency.

Continue reading...
title: Polls open in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – UK politics live

author: Ben Quinn
description:
Teddy Young, 24, from Bedfordshire, charged with obtaining information to benefit foreign power

A member of the Royal Navy has been charged under Britain’s National Security Act with offences including obtaining information to benefit a foreign power.

Teddy Young, 24, had arrested at his home address in Bedfordshire on 6 October after an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London (CTPL).

Continue reading...
title: Royal Navy serviceman arrested under National Security Act

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Sales rise 2% to £33.8bn in the past six months, helped by strong trade online

  • Business live – latest updates

Tesco has raised its annual profit forecast as the supermarket group said consumer confidence has remained relatively resilient this year despite ongoing geopolitical tensions “creating uncertainty”.

The UK’s biggest grocer said sales rose just 2% to £33.8bn in the first six months of its financial year but underlying profit was up 6.5% to £1.8bn.

Continue reading...
title: Tesco lifts profit forecast and says consumer confidence is resilient

author: Ben Smee
description:
Court hears police attended Wood’s Victorian home over a similar allegation about three years ago, but the woman had not complained then out of ‘fear of retribution’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman who was allegedly choked and assaulted by the former Bachelor star Sam Wood told police she “thought she was going to die”, a Queensland court heard on Thursday.

The court also heard that police in Victoria had attended Wood’s home in relation to a similar incident about three years ago, but that the woman had not wanted to make a complaint at that time out of “fear of retribution”.

Wood, a 46-year-old wellness influencer from Melbourne, was denied bail in a Queensland court on Thursday and will be held in
title: Bachelor star Sam Wood denied bail as police allege he choked woman until she ‘thought she would die’

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: A youth-led movement is protesting crumbling school buildings and teacher shortages while turning adult focus onto wider educational inequalities

Good morning. In my experience, at any protest, the most memorable and encapsulating slogans are always the ones written by hand with marker pen on cardboard placards.

“School is a right, not a privilege,” read one such sign held aloft by a student in Paris, where huge youth protests over the state of high school education have brought tens of thousands of young people and adults on to the streets, with further strikes planned today.

UK politics | Kemi Badenoch has announced that the Conservatives would abolish inheritance tax on family homes if elected, prompting criticism that she is prioritising cutting taxes for the rich.<
title: Thursday briefing: Why young people are taking to the streets across France

author: Penry Buckley and Jordyn Beazley
description:
Police watchdog says Mal Lanyon’s timing in raising the issue was ‘regrettable’ and led to delays

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales police commissioner made a last-minute bid to hold hearings into Sydney’s anti-Herzog protest behind closed doors, delaying the inquiry, the police watchdog has revealed.

The Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (Lecc) has said that its inquiry into the February protest at Sydney’s town hall, launched after widespread allegations of police brutality, would go ahead this month with a mix of public and private examinations, saying the timing of issues r
title: NSW police commissioner made last-minute bid to hold closed-door hearings into Sydney anti-Herzog protest

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Youngest complainant in trial alleges Jones put his tongue in his mouth and touched him on the bottom during visit to shock jock’s property

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

  • Listen to the podcast Alan Jones on Trial

An alleged teenage victim of Alan Jones has denied his family tried to deceive the broadcaster and get as much money out of him as they could during a tense cross-examination in a Sydney court.

Asked whether he was intent on getting as much financial assistance as he could from the former 2GB host, the witness replied: “That is a lie.”
title: ‘That is a lie’: alleged Alan Jones victim denies family tried to get money out of broadcaster, court hears

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
Responding to a Guardian report that revealed thousands of tonnes of fuel was transported to Russia, Seoul said it was investigating the cases

South Korea will take legal action if it finds that shipments of fuel from its ports to Russia broke domestic law, the government has said, responding to a Guardian report on the trade.

The government, in a statement issued by the foreign and trade ministries and the customs service, said that it is “checking additional information concerning the loading cases reported by the Guardian” and “if the verification establishes that our laws and regulations have been violated, it plans to act in accordance with the law”.

Continue reading...
title: South Korea threatens legal action if fuel shipments to Russia found to have broken law

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Former NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to the February 2024 murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Sydney

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Photographs of the decomposed bodies of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies have been shown to 15 jurors tasked with deciding whether the two men were murdered.

Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to the February 2024 murders of Baird, 26, and Davies, 29.

Continue reading...
title: Jurors in Beau Lamarre-Condon murder case shown photos of decomposed bodies

author: Jonathan Barrett
description:
Sources say Firmus is slashing its price and may even shelve initial public offering altogether

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The momentum behind Firmus Technologies’ high-flying valuation is showing severe cracks just weeks out from its anticipated ASX debut.

Multiple sources briefed on the matter told Guardian Australia the AI datacentre company is slashing its valuation to entice sceptical investors – or may even shelve its initial public offering altogether.

Cont
title: Datacentre company Firmus’s high flying valuation may be coming back down to earth ahead of expected ASX debut
